EC 1.4.3.10. Soluble dimeric flavoprotein, 50 kDa subunits, non-covalent FAD. Putrescine is its best substrate of those tested. kcat/Km = 3.17 /uM/s, six times DhaPAO on DAS. Km 8.2 uM sits inside the urinary clinical range, which no other module here manages. Accepts longer polyamines, so spermidine and spermine are expected cross-reactants; short diamines and monoamines inhibit. t1/2 at 50 C is 2 h.

Monomeric sarcosine oxidase, Protein ID BAA03967, MW 43836 Da with FAD. Table 2 wild type: Km 17 +/- 2.6 mM, kcat 25 +/- 2.9 /s, specific activity 29 +/- 3.4 U/mg. kcat/Km = 0.0015 /uM/s, the weakest module in this table by three orders. Urinary sarcosine is micromolar, so the analyte sits about 1800x below Km: first order and far from saturation, but it needs correspondingly more enzyme. Assay by 4-aminoantipyrine/peroxidase at pH 8.0, 37 C.

EC 1.1.3.17. Table 1, fully oxidised FAD: kcat 61 +/- 6 /s, Ka 1.7 +/- 0.3 mM, kcat/Ka 36000 +/- 6400 /M/s. The paper reports Ka, the Michaelis constant for choline at saturating oxygen in a sequential mechanism, not a classical Km; below saturation the relevant quantity is kcat/Ka = 0.036 /uM/s, which is what this screen uses. KO2 703 +/- 102 uM. Measured at pH 7, 25 C.

EC 1.1.3.2, FMN-dependent. Wild type: kcat 88 +/- 2 /s, Km 0.50 +/- 0.10 mM, kcat/Km 176 +/- 31.2 /mM/s = 0.176 /uM/s. Measured air-saturated at [O2] 250 uM, pH 6.5, 20 C; Km for O2 about 51 uM, so oxygen was near-saturating. Tyr215 variants are published if a tighter Km is wanted: Y215F has Km 0.13 mM at kcat 22 /s.

No numerical Kd in this paper. Two web searches on 2026-10-06 found none elsewhere either, but that is a failed search rather than proof of absence. Gel-shift titration used 0, 10, 50 and 100 mM putrescine, roughly three orders of magnitude above urinary clinical levels. Spermidine had little or no effect, so selectivity over spermidine is plausible. The type A route to putrescine (PuORh) is quantified and this one is not.

AraC-family sarcosine-responsive activator of the sox operon. Confirmed sarcosine-responsive by beta-galactosidase reporter at 1 mM sarcosine and by EMSA, but no numerical ligand Kd is reported. Induction is specific: glycine betaine, dimethylglycine, glycine and pyruvate all fail to induce, so selectivity looks good but is unquantified. Activator, not a derepressed repressor.

Repressor; choline binding stimulates BetI-DNA complex formation. Reported Kd range 90-120 nM; the low end is entered and the range recorded here rather than averaged. Measured at pH 9.0 in 10 mM Tris-HCl with binding on ice, far from assay conditions, so the number should be treated as an order of magnitude. The only type B module in this table with any numerical constant.

Native lactate-responsive regulator. The cited paper characterises an engineered fluorescent sensor built on the LldR binding domain, not LldR acting as a transcription factor, so its Kd belongs to the fusion protein and is not entered here. No Kd for LldR as a repressor was found.
